This entry represents beta-propeller domains of echinoderm microtubule-associated protein (EMAP)-like (EML) proteins [[cite:PUB00103956]], a family of proteins that contribute to formation of the mitotic spindle and interphase microtubule network [[cite:PUB00103956]]. In these proteins, the beta-propellers are intimately associated as a pair which was defined as tandem atypical propeller in EMLs (TAPE) domain. There is a hydrophobic core between the propellers which corresponds the HELP motif ([pfam:PF03451]) that contributes blades 1 and 14 buried at the interface and joints them [[cite:PUB00103956]]. This model completes the second beta-propeller of the TAPE pair in EMLs. In some members, such as EML5 and EML6, there are three TAPE pairs. The first beta-propeller of the pair is represented in [pfam:PF23409].
This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in FAM234A/B proteins from mammals, whose function is unknown.

This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in HPS5, a component of the biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles complex-2 (BLOC-2) [[cite:PUB00043624]] and which has a role in the endo-lysosomal dynamics of skin fibroblasts [[cite:PUB00155526]]. Its mutation or absence has been linked to eye-colour mutations in insects [[cite:PUB00085365]] and Hermansky-Pudlak type 5 syndrome (HPS-5) in mammals, a disease characterized by defects in lysosome-related organelles such as melanosomes and platelet dense granules [[cite:PUB00155527]]. This entry also represents the beta-propeller domain found in the tectonin beta-propeller repeat-containing protein 2 (TCPR2).
This family represents a group of proteins mainly from halobacteria, including HVO_0234 from Haloferax volcanii ([swissprot:D4GZH9]). Members are predicted to adopt a beta -propeller configuration.

IFT122 is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT140) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00101516]]. This entry represents the first beta-propeller of IFT122, which is a crucial subunit for IFT-A integrity [[cite:PUB00155528]].

IFT122 is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT140) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00101516]]. This entry represents the second beta-propeller of IFT122, which is a crucial subunit for IFT-A integrity [[cite:PUB00155528]].

IFT140 is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT122) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00089704]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00089704]]. The beta-propeller domains of IFT140 contact the beta-propeller domains of IFT121 from the adjacent complex [[cite:PUB00155528]]. This entry represents the first beta-propeller of IFT140.

IFT140 is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT122) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00089704],[cite:PUB00155528]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00155528]]. The beta-propeller domains of IFT140 contact the beta-propeller domains of IFT121 from the adjacent complex [[cite:PUB00089704]]. This entry represents the second beta-propeller of IFT140.

This entry represents the second beta-propeller of the Intraflagellar transport protein 80 homolog (IFT80) from human and related proteins. IFT80 is a component of the intraflagellar transport (IFT) complex B, which is essential for the development and maintenance of motile and sensory cilia. It is required for initiation of the ciliary axoneme [[cite:PUB00155530]]. It has an unique architecture consisting of two beta-propellers followed by an alpha-solenoid structure [[cite:PUB00155530]]. This beta-propeller is involved in dimerization together with the alpha-solenoid[[cite:PUB00155530]].

This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found mainly in plant inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatases (IP5P), such as Type I IP5P12/IP5PC and IP5P13/IP5PD and Type II IP5P14/IP5PE and IP5P15/IP5PF from Arabidopsis thaliana. IP5Ps have different functions, including the degradation of phosphoinositides in the signalling pathways of various cellular processes such as Ca2+ release, abscisic acid signalling and vesicle trafficking, among others [[cite:PUB00155531]]. In the case of IP5P13, the beta propeller domain interacts with the sucrose non-fermenting-1-related kinase (SnRK1.1) in order to achieve a regulatory role linking inositol, sugar and stress signalling [[cite:PUB00134029]].

This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found in F-box proteins KIB1-4, from Arabidopsis thaliana, and similar plant proteins. This domain adopts a beta-propeller structure with 6 blades and is often found in association with F-box domain ([pfam:PF00646]). KIB1-4 are ubiquitin ligases that act as essential positive regulators in brassinosteroid signalling, mediating the ubiquitination, substrate interaction and degradation of GSK3 kinase BIN2 [[cite:PUB00094297]].

This entry represents the beta-propeller found at the C-terminal in Leucine-rich repeat serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (LRRK2) from eukaryotes. LRRK2 is a serine/threonine-protein kinase which phosphorylates a broad range of proteins involved in multiple processes such as neuronal plasticity, primary ciliogenesis, autophagy, and vesicle trafficking [[cite:PUB00155495],[cite:PUB00155496],[cite:PUB00155497],[cite:PUB00155498]]. Mutations in LRRK2 are the most common genetic cause of Parkinson's disease (PD)[[cite:PUB00155495]].The beta-propeller domain is suggested to mediate LRRK2 dimerization and autophosphorylation, and plays an important role in neurotoxicity associated to LRRK2 PD mutations [[cite:PUB00130288],[cite:PUB00155499],[cite:PUB00155500]].

This domain is found at the N-terminal end of human Nucleolar protein 10 (NOL10) and similar eukaryotic sequences. This domain is normally found N-terminal to [pfam:PF23097]. This entry includes a entire beta-propeller structure and two alpha -helices.

This entry represents the beta-propeller found in the nuclear pore complex proteins 159 and 146 (NUP159 and NUP146) from yeast and NUP214 from animals. These proteins play a critical role in mRNA nuclear export [[cite:PUB00155532],[cite:PUB00155533]]. Mutations in the beta-propeller domain abolish binding to DP5 in yeast [[cite:PUB00032431]] or DDX19 in humans [[cite:PUB00052000]], dead box helicases required for nuclear pore export function.

This entry represents the beta-propeller found at the C-terminal of NACHT and WD repeat domain-containing protein 2 (NWD2) from human and similar eukaryotic proteins. The function of these proteins is not yet known.

This entry represents the first beta-propeller found at the N-terminal of Protein rigor mortis (RIG) from Drosophila melanogaster. RIG is a nuclear receptor-interacting protein required for the response to steroid hormone ecdysone during larval development [[cite:PUB00155010]]. This domain acts as a specific protein-protein interaction domain. Also included in this entry as partial matches are orthologues Gem-associated protein 5 (GEMI5) from animals. GEMI5 is a component of the survival of motor neurons (SMN) complex, that binds small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs). The SMN complex assembles the heptameric Sm protein core on snRNAs and plays a critical role in the biogenesis of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) [[cite:PUB00155534],[cite:PUB00155535]].

This entry represents the second beta-propeller found in Protein rigor mortis (RIG) from Drosophila melanogaster. RIG is a nuclear receptor-interacting protein required for the response to steroid hormone ecdysone during larval development. This domain acts as a specific protein-protein interaction domain [[cite:PUB00155010]]. Also included in this entry are orthologues Gem-associated protein 5 (GEMI5) from animals. GEMI5 is a component of the survival of motor neurons (SMN) complex. The beta-propellers in GEMI5 bind small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) playing a critical role in the assembly of the heptameric Sm protein core on snRNAs and the biogenesis of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) [[cite:PUB00155534],[cite:PUB00155536]].

This entry represents the beta-propeller found towards the N-terminus of RSE1/SF3B3/DDB1/CPSF1/CFT1 proteins from eukaryotes, which share a domain architecture consisting of three beta-propeller. Members of the family have diverse functions, primarily related to RNA/DNA binding. Pre-mRNA-splicing factor RSE1 plays an important role in the spliceosome, a complex that removes introns from pre-mRNAs [[cite:PUB00155537]]. Its orthologue, splicing factor 3B subunit 3 (SF3B3) also forms part of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle (snRNP) and has been identified as part of the SAGA transcriptional coactivator complex in Drosophila melanogaster [[cite:PUB00155538]]. Also included in this entry is DNA damage -binding protein 1 (DDB1), which is both involved in the recognition and repair of UV-induced DNA damage, as part of the UV-DDB complex, and in protein ubiquitination, as part of the DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) complex [[cite:PUB00155539],[cite:PUB00155540]]. Additionally, this family includes cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 1 (CPSF1) and its orthologue protein CFT1, both involved in the cleavage and polyadenylation of pre-mRNAs [[cite:PUB00007715],[cite:PUB00155541]].

This entry represents the beta-propeller domain found at the C-terminal of SCAP proteins, key regulators of lipid homeostasis in cells. It acts as a cholesterol sensor and escort for SREBP, therefore, when cholesterol levels are low, SCAP binds to SREBP and facilitates its transport from the ER to the Golgi, where it undergoes proteolytic cleavage and activates it, leading to its activation and translocation to the nucleus to activate the transcription of genes involved in cholesterol synthesis. This domain is involved in the interaction with SREBP [1.2].

This entry represents the second WD40 beta-propeller found in WD repeat-containing protein 90, identified in animals, and the homologue protein POC16 found in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. WDR90 is proposed to be localised in the centriole and required for ciliogenesis [[cite:PUB00090986]]. The similarities between WDR90 and the flagellar inner B-microtubule protein FAP52/WDR16 lead to the proposal that the WD40 domains of WDR90 might be located within the B-microtubule of the centriole triplet [[cite:PUB00155545]].

WDR35 (also known as IFT121) is a component of the IFT-A complex, which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00101516]]. Proteins in this entry are part of the non-core subcomplex, together with IFT43 and IFT139 [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. This entry represents the second beta-propeller of WDR35. Knock-out WDR35 cells showed defective retrograde trafficking within cilia [[cite:PUB00101516]].

This entry represents a beta-propeller domain found at N-terminal of WDR35 (in which corresponds to the first one) and TULP4 proteins. TULP4 may be a substrate-recognition component of a SCF-like ECS (Elongin-Cullin-SOCS-box protein) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex. WDR35 (also known as IFT121) is a component of the IFT-A complex, which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of beta-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00101516]]. Proteins in this entry are part of the non-core subcomplex, together with IFT43 and IFT139 [[cite:PUB00155528],[cite:PUB00101516]]. This entry represents the second beta-propeller of WDR35. Knock-out WDR35 cells showed defective retrograde trafficking within cilia [[cite:PUB00101516]].

Pfam_Description: EGF-like domain-containing protein ComC first beta-sandwich
Pfam_name: EGF-like domain-containing protein ComC first beta-sandwich
Pfam_description: This entry represents the first beta-sandwich domain found in EGF-like domain containing protein ComC from amoebas. This protein regulates aggregation, inhibiting lagC and activating lagD expression [[cite:PUB00154458]]. The function of this domain is unknown.

Pfam_Description: EGF-like domain-containing protein ComC second beta-sandwich
Pfam_name: EGF-like domain-containing protein ComC second beta-sandwich
Pfam_description: This entry represents the second beta-sandwich domain found in EGF-like domain containing protein ComC from amoebas. This protein regulates aggregation, inhibiting lagC and activating lagD expression [[cite:PUB00154458]]. The function of this domain is unknown.

Protein defective in exine formation DEX1 is a factor required for proper pollen wall formation in Arabidopsis thaliana and other plant sequences. This entry represents the beta sandwich found towards the C-terminus of DEX1 in plants. Mutations in DEX1 are associated with changes in the microspore membrane and primexine formation, which disrupt normal deposition of sporopollenin. DEX1 is suggested to be a either a component of the primexine matrix or the ER and participates in the assembly of primexine precursors [[cite:PUB00098326]]. DEX1 has been identified as a Ca2+ binding protein involved in regulating rice tapetal cell degradation and pollen formation [[cite:PUB00098579]].

This domain is found in eukaryotes, and is approximately 40 amino acids in length. It is found associated with [pfam:PF00646], [pfam:PF00400]. The protein that contains this domain functions as a ubiquitin ligase. Ubiquitination is required to direct proteins towards the proteasome for degradation. This protein is part of the WD40 class of F box proteins. The D domain of these F box proteins is involved in mediating the dimerisation of the protein. Dimerisation is necessary to polyubiquitinate substrates so this D domain is vital in directing substrates towards the proteasome for degradation.

This entry represents the beta-trefoil domain found in endo-acting ulvan lyase from bacteria. Ulvan lyases degrade the main polysaccharide component of green seaweed cell walls [[cite:PUB00093668],[cite:PUB00155552]]. This domain binds to ulvan [[cite:PUB00155553]].

This domain is the second all-beta domain from beta galactosidase enzymes which has a jelly roll fold [[cite:PUB00031444]]. These enzymes consist of a TIM-barrel catalytic domain and two all-beta domains (ABD), ABD1 is represented in [pfam:PF21317] and this entry represents ABD2.

Beta-galactosidases belong to glycosyl hydrolase 35 family (GH35) which catalyse the cleaveage of beta-linked terminal galactosyl residues from gangliosides, glycoproteins, and glycosaminoglycans. These proteins consist of a catalytic TIM-barrel and two all-beta domains (ABD1 and ABD2) [[cite:PUB00152061],[cite:PUB00152062],[cite:PUB00152063],[cite:PUB00152064],[cite:PUB00152065]]. This entry represents the first all-beta domain ABD1. ABD2 is represented in [pfam:PF13364].

This is the second domain of the five-domain beta-galactosidase enzyme that altogether catalyses the hydrolysis of beta(1-3) and beta(1-4) galactosyl bonds in oligosaccharides as well as the inverse reaction of enzymatic condensation and trans-glycosylation. This domain is made up of 16 antiparallel beta-strands and an alpha-helix at its C terminus. The fold of this domain appears to be unique. In addition, the last seven strands of the domain form a subdomain with an immunoglobulin-like (I-type Ig) fold in which the first strand is divided between the two beta-sheets. In penicillin spp this strand is interrupted by a 12-residue insertion which forms an additional edge-strand to the second beta-sheet of the sub-domain. The remainder of the second domain forms a series of beta-hairpins at its N terminus, four strands of which are contiguous with part of the Ig-like sub-domain, forming in total a seven-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet. This domain is associated with family Glyco_hydro_35, [pfam:PF01301], which is N-terminal to it, but itself has no metazoan members.

This is the third domain of the five-domain beta-galactosidase enzyme that altogether catalyses the hydrolysis of beta(1-3) and beta(1-4) galactosyl bonds in oligosaccharides as well as the inverse reaction of enzymatic condensation and trans-glycosylation. This domain has an Ig-like fold [[cite:PUB00031444]].

Beta-galactosidase belongs to Glycoside hydrolase family 35 [[cite:PUB00031444],[cite:PUB00058868],[cite:PUB00152061],[cite:PUB00151854],[cite:PUB00152062]]. This entry represents the galactose-binding domain.

betaPIX_CC is the very C-terminal coiled-coil region of betaPIX or p21-activated kinase interacting exchange factor proteins. The coiled-coil runs from residues 589-646 in UniProtKB:G31IU6, and the PDZ-binding site is the final eight residues immediately downstream. The coiled-coil trimerises and thus exposes three potential PZD-binding surfaces, although only one of these is maximally used. One of the C-terminal ends of the coiled-coil forms an extensive beta-sheet interaction with the Shank PDZ, while the other two ends are not involved in ligand binding and form random coils. Thus the coiled-coil domain allows multimerisation of betaPIX that is vital for its physiological functions. betaPIX and the Shank/ProSAP protein form a complex that acts as a protein scaffold for integrating signalling pathways and regulating postsynaptic structure [[cite:PUB00076307]].** Forced reload
This region contains a parallel beta helix region that shares some similarity with Pectate lyases.

Pfam_Description: Beta helix repeat of Inulin fructotransferase
Pfam_name: Beta helix repeat of Inulin fructotransferase
Pfam_description: This region contains a right-handed parallel beta helix repeat unit found in Inulin fructotransferase [[cite:PUB00047720]]. This Pfam entry includes sequences not found by [pfam:PF13229].
This is a family derived from microsporidia-specific proteins. There is homology to the beta-lactamase domain.

Members of this family comprise secreted bacterial proteins containing C-terminal beta-propeller domain distantly related to WD-40 repeats. Jpred secondary-structure prediction shows family to be a series of 4 short beta-strands, characteristic of beta-propeller families.
This family includes the beta protein from Bacteriophage T4, [swissprot:P13057]. Beta protein prevents the gop protein, [swissprot:P13058], from killing the bacterial host cell [[cite:PUB00057864]].
This family includes an N-terminal helix-turn-helix domain.

This family is named after Bet v 1, the major birch pollen allergen. This protein belongs to family 10 of plant pathogenesis-related proteins (PR-10), cytoplasmic proteins of 15-17 kd that are wide-spread among dicotyledonous plants [[cite:PUB00056876]]. In recent years, a number of diverse plant proteins with low sequence similarity to Bet v 1 was identified. A classification by sequence similarity yielded several subfamilies related to PR-10 [[cite:PUB00053295]]: - Pathogenesis-related proteins PR-10: These proteins were identified as major tree pollen allergens in birch and related species (hazel, alder), as plant food allergens expressed in high levels in fruits, vegetables and seeds (apple, celery, hazelnut), and as pathogenesis-related proteins whose expression is induced by pathogen infection, wounding, or abiotic stress. Hyp-1 ([swissprot:Q8H1L1]), an enzyme involved in the synthesis of the bioactive naphthodianthrone hypericin in St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) also belongs to this family. Most of these proteins were found in dicotyledonous plants. In addition, related sequences were identified in monocots and conifers. - Cytokinin-specific binding proteins: These legume proteins bind cytokinin plant hormones [[cite:PUB00047452]]. - (S)-Norcoclaurine synthases are enzymes catalysing the condensation of dopamine and 4-hydroxyphenylacetaldehyde to (S)-norcoclaurine, the first committed step in the biosynthesis of benzylisoquinoline alkaloids such as morphine [[cite:PUB00056877]]. -Major latex proteins and ripening-related proteins are proteins of unknown biological function that were first discovered in the latex of opium poppy (Papaver somniferum) and later found to be upregulated during ripening of fruits such as strawberry and cucumber [[cite:PUB00056877]]. The occurrence of Bet v 1-related proteins is confined to seed plants with the exception of a cytokinin-binding protein from the moss Physcomitrella patens ([swissprot:Q9AXI3]).

This is a family of transcription elongation factors which includes those referred to as Bex proteins as well as those named TCEAL7. Bex1 was shown to be a novel link between neurotrophin signalling, the cell cycle, and neuronal differentiation, suggesting it might function by coordinating internal cellular states with the ability of cells to respond to external signals [[cite:PUB00073473]]. TCEAL7 has been shown negatively to regulate the NF-kappaB pathway, hence being important in ovarian cancer as it one of the genes frequently downregulated in this cancer. A closely related protein, TFIIS/TCEA, found in [pfam:PF07500] is involved in transcription elongation and transcript fidelity. TFIIS/TCEA promotes 3' endoribonuclease activity of RNA polymerase II (pol II) and allows pol II to bypass transcript pause or 'arrest' during elongation process. It is thus possible that BEX is also acting in this way [[cite:PUB00073473]].

This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in bacterial 1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzymes, such as TTHA1902 from Thermus thermophilus and TK1436 from Thermococcus kodakarensis, which belong to the glycoside hydrolase family 57 (GH57). These enzymes catalyse the formation of branch points in alpha-glucans by cleavage of an alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond and subsequent transfer of the cleaved-off oligosaccharide to a new alpha-1,6 position. This is an alpha-helical domain composed of a four alpha-helical bundle. It plays a role in the formation of the active-site cleft, being essential for substrate binding and catalysis [[cite:PUB00090452],[cite:PUB00058786]].
This domain is found at the C-terminal end of BF9343_1606 from Bacteroides fragilis. This domain, which shows an all-alpha structure, is associated with [pfam:PF12985].

Pfam_Description: Biogenesis factor required for ATP synthase 1, C-terminal domain
Pfam_name: Biogenesis factor required for ATP synthase 1, C-terminal domain
Pfam_description: This domain is predominantly found at the C-terminal end of proteins from cyanobacteria and plants, including Biogenesis factor required for ATP synthase 1 (BFA1, [swissprot:F4J1U2]) from Arabidopsis thaliana. BFA1 promotes the assembly of the CF1 subcomplex of the chloroplast ATP synthase by specifically interacting with the gamma and beta subunits. This domain consists of ten beta-sheets and one alpha- helix forming a typical beta-barrel, which locates perpendicularly to [pfam:PF12204] [[cite:PUB00100989]].

This domain is found in sequences from Drosophila sp., including the transcriptional cofactor Bfc ([[swissprot:Q9W0I5]], which adopts a C2-like fold. Bfc is a transcriptional cofactor involved in efferocytosis. Together with Srp mediates expression of the phagocytic receptor crq/croquemort in response to apoptotic cells, and is up-regulated by crq/croquemort in a positive feedback mechanism. Bfc is also involved in macrophage engulfment and clearance of apoptotic cells during embryogenesis [[cite:PUB00153832]].

Pfam_Description: Metal-independent restriction enzyme BfiI DNA binding domain
Pfam_name: Metal-independent restriction enzyme BfiI DNA binding domain
Pfam_description: This domain is found in the metal-independent restriction enzyme BfiI present in Bacillus firmus. This domain is found in the C-terminal of the protein and is responsible for DNA binding. The domain exhibits a beta-barrel-like structure similar to the effector DNA-binding domain of the Mg2+ dependent restriction enzyme EcoRII and to the B3-like DNA-binding domain of plant transcription factors [[cite:PUB00039849]].
This family of proteins have a repetitive structure composed of pairs of beta strands. In this family the proteins usually have four copies of the beta hairpin repeat.
This family of proteins have a repetitive structure composed of pairs of beta strands. In this family the proteins usually have five copies of the beta hairpin repeat.

This family of proteins have a repetitive structure composed of pairs of beta strands. In this family the proteins usually have six copies of the beta hairpin repeat with a central alpha helix in the barrel.

This entry represents the bifunctional nuclease (BFN) domain which is specific to bacteria and plant organisms. It has both RNase and DNase activities [[cite:PUB00057454]]. The dimer of the BFN domain forms a wedge, each monomer being a basic triangular shape. The BFN domain is composed of an eight-stranded, distorted beta-sheet consisting of a four-stranded antiparallel beta-sheet, and a four-stranded mixed beta-sheet. This domain can be found in M. tuberculosis Carbon monoxide resistance (Cor) proteins. Cor consists entirely of this domain with homologues in a variety of organisms, including most mycobacteria, Bacteroides sp., Chlamydia sp., Streptomyces sp., and Rhodococcussp. One of the homologs from Oryza minuta protein OmBBD was reported to exhibit DNase and RNAse activity in vitro [[cite:PUB00057454]]. OmBBD carries a C-terminal UvrB domain that is absent in the mycobacterial sequences. UvrB is one component of the UvrABC endonuclease system. Hence, it was proposed that OmBBD's observed nuclease activity may come not from this domain but from an interaction of the C-terminal UvrB with the catalytic UvrC nuclease [[cite:PUB00109344]].

This domain is found in Beta-galactosidase from Streptococcus pneumoniae (BgaA) and similar bacterial sequences. BgaA is specific for terminal galactose residues beta-1-4 linked to glucose or N-acetylglucosamine. It is involved in pneumococcal growth, resistance to opsonophagocytic killing, and adherence. This entry represents two non-enzymatic carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) that mediate adherence to the host cell surface displayed lactose or N-acetyllactosamine. Each of these CBMs folds into a beta-sandwich fold comprising opposing sheets of 4- and 5-antiparallel beta-strands [[cite:PUB00151854]].
This domain comprises the small chain of dimeric beta-galactosidases [ec:3.2.1.23]. This domain is also found in single chain beta-galactosidase.

This domain is located centrally in BH1974 protein from Alkalihalobacillus halodurans and similar bacterial proteins. It is found C-terminal to [pfam:PF02625] and N-terminal to [pfam:PF13478] and shows an alpha-beta structure.
The BH3 domain is a short motif known to bind to Bcl-xLs. This interaction is important in apoptosis.
This short domain is found in the Rad4 protein. This domain binds to DNA [[cite:PUB00044171]].
This short domain is found in the Rad4 protein. This domain binds to DNA [[cite:PUB00044171]].
This short domain is found in the Rad4 protein. This domain binds to DNA [[cite:PUB00044171]].

Pfam_Description: bHLH-MYC and R2R3-MYB transcription factors N-terminal
Pfam_name: bHLH-MYC and R2R3-MYB transcription factors N-terminal
Pfam_description: This is the N-terminal region of a family of MYB and MYC transcription factors. The DNA-binding HLH domain is further downstream, [pfam:PF00010]. Members of the MYB and MYC family regulate the biosynthesis of phenylpropanoids in several plant species (DOI:10.1007/s11295-009-0232-y).

Pfam_Description: Plant bHLH transcription factor, ACT-like domain
Pfam_name: Plant bHLH transcription factor, ACT-like domain
Pfam_description: This entry represents an ACT-like domain found at the C-terminal of plant transcription factors, such as transcription factor GLABRA 3 from Arabidopsis and the bHLH transcription factor (swissprot:A0A060CUZ2) from maize, which is associated with bHLH domains. This domain association is unique to the plantae kingdom [[cite:PUB00153833]]. Phylogenetic analysis show that the association of ACT-like and bHLH domains occurred early in Plantae by recruitment of an ACT-like domain in a common ancestor with widely distributed ACT DOMAIN REPEAT (ACR) genes by an ancestral bHLH gene. The functional significance of this association relies on the homodimer formation of ACT-like domains that negatively affects DNA binding of the associated bHLH domains [[cite:PUB00153833]]. For some bHLH transcription factors with the C-terminal ACT-like domain, such as Arabidopsis SPEECHLESS and MUTE, the ACT-like domain serves as heterodimerisation selectivity interface.

The founding member of this family is the bHLH domain of Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha that functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the adaptive response to hypoxia [[cite:PUB00107570],[cite:PUB00107571]]. This domain also found in other transcription factors such as Single-minded homolog 1 (SIM1), Neuronal PAS domain-containing protein 3 (NPAS3), Endothelial PAS domain-containing protein 1 (EPAS1) etc.

This bHLH domain is found in the family of Increased Leaf Inclination (ILI) family of atypical bHLH transcription factors in rice. The members of this family ILI1/2/3/4/5/6/7 lack the basic region for DNA binding and have been implicated in brassinosteroids signaling [[cite:PUB00155554]]. This domain is also found in Arabidopsis thaliana Paclobutrazol Resistance proteins PRE1/2/3/4/5/6 that have a regulatory role in various aspects of gibberellin-dependent growth and development [[cite:PUB00095759]].

This bHLH domain is found in Arabidopsis thaliana Transcription factor LONESOME HIGHWAY (LHW) and related proteins from plants. LHW is a transcription activator that regulates root development. Mutations in this protein eliminate bilateral symmetry and reduce the number of cells in the center of the root, resulting in roots with only single xylem and phloem poles [[cite:PUB00078281]].

This bHLH domain is found in the family of nuclear receptor coactivators NCOA1, NCOA2, and NCOA3. The NCOAs bind to nuclear hormone receptors in a ligand-dependent manner and mediate the transcriptional activation of the downstream target genes in response to hormones, metabolites, xenobiotics, and drugs.

This bHLH domain is found in the family of Neuronal PAS domain-containing protein 4 (NPAS4). NPAS4 is a transcription factor expressed in neurons of the brain that regulates the excitatory-inhibitory balance within neural circuits and is required for contextual memory in the hippocampus [[cite:PUB00155557]]. It binds to DNA but efficient DNA binding requires dimerization with another bHLH protein, such as ARNT, ARNT2 or BMAL1 [[cite:PUB00149730],[cite:PUB00155558]].

Pfam_Description: Period circadian protein homolog bHLH-like domain
Stimulated by retinoic acid gene 8 protein bHLH domain
Pfam_name: Stimulated by retinoic acid gene 8 protein bHLH domain
Pfam_description: This bHLH domain is found in the family of Stimulated by retinoic acid gene 8 protein (STRA8). This protein is required for the transition into meiosis for both female and male germ cells [[cite:PUB00079035],[cite:PUB00079036]]. In female germ cells, it acts as a key effector of the meiotic program and is required for premeiotic DNA replication and subsequent events in meiotic prophase [[cite:PUB00155559]].

BibA, a group B streptococcus (GBS) surface protein, has been shown to protect the pathogen from phagocytic killing by sequestering a complement inhibitor: C4b-binding protein (C4BP) [[cite:PUB00151658]]. This entry represents a three helical repeated domain in this protein.

Pfam_Description: Protein bicaudal C homolog 1, KH-like domain
Pfam_name: Protein bicaudal C homolog 1, KH-like domain
Pfam_description: This domain is found in the homologues of human Protein bicaudal C homolog 1 (Bicc1). Bicc1 is an RNA-binding protein composed of three KH and two KH-like domains that are linked by an intervening sequence to a C-terminal SAM domain. Bicc1 acts as a negative regulator of Wnt signaling [[cite:PUB00103533]]. It is also involved in regulating gene expression during embryonic development. Bicc1 binds the 3' UTRs of the target mRNAs via KH domains, whereas self-polymerization of its SAM domain mediates recruitment to large cytoplasmic foci for translational silencing [[cite:PUB00148472]]. This entry represents the Bicc1 KH-like domains.

BicD proteins consist of three coiled-coiled domains and are involved in dynein-mediated minus end-directed transport from the Golgi apparatus to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). For full functioning they bind with GSK-3beta [pfam:PF05350] to maintain the anchoring of microtubules to the centromere. It appears that amino-acid residues 437-617 of BicD and the kinase activity of GSK-3 are necessary for the formation of a complex between BicD and GSK-3beta in intact cells [[cite:PUB00044172]].

BID is a member of the BCL-2 superfamily of proteins are key regulators of programmed cell death, hence this family is related to [pfam:PF00452] . BID is a pro-apoptotic member of the Bcl-2 superfamily and as such posses the ability to target intracellular membranes and contains the BH3 death domain. The activity of BID is regulated by a Caspase 8-mediated cleavage event, exposing the BH3 domain and significantly changing the surface charge and hydrophobicity, which causes a change of cellular localisation [[cite:PUB00012361]].
This family consists of bacterial domains with an Ig-like fold. Members of this family are found in a variety of bacterial surface proteins.
This presumed domain is found repeat in bacterial cell surface proteins.
Presumed domain found as tandem repeats of high sequence identity in bacterial cell surface proteins.
Presumed domain found as tandem repeats of high sequence identity in bacterial cell surface proteins.
This bacterial Ig-like domain shows some similarity to [pfam:PF12690] suggesting it may act as a protease inhibitor similar to B. subtilis BsuPI.

This entry represents BIg21(Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 21) found in InvasinE (InvE). Invasins are members of the inverse autotransporter (IAT) family also referred to as type Ve secretion system. In general, they consist of an N-terminal beta-barrel-like domain, which is responsible for attachment of invasin to the outer membrane region of bacteria, repetitive Immunoglobuli-like (Ig) domains, which vary significantly in number among all the invasins, and the C-terminal domain/adhesion domain (AD) [pfam:PF05689], which provides invasins with the specificity to bind to its host target molecules. The overall structure of InvE shows that it comprises of three domain architecture in which the domains BIg20 (Bacterial Immunoglobulin-like 20) and BIg21 adopt two layer beta-sandwich fold resembling eukaryotic members of Immunoglobulin-superfamily (IgSF), while the AD is a globular, alpha/beta-domain. The structure of BIg21 belongs to the I2 set of IgSF with a unique modification in the C-E interstrand loop, important for its interaction with AD. BIg21 and AD form a functional super-domain as well, necessary to target the host receptor [[cite:PUB00101290]].
This presumed domain is found at the C-terminus of BIG2 the brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein. The function of this region is unknown.

This family catalyses the synthesis of thymidine monophosphate (dTMP) from deoxyuridine monophosphate (dUMP). The physiological co-substrate has not yet been identified. Previous designation of this famliy as being thymidylate synthase from one paper, [cite:PUB00075419], has been shown to be erroneous [[cite:PUB00057368]]. The proteins are uncharacterised.

EKR is a short, 33 residue, domain found in bacterial and some lower eukaryotic species which lies between a POR (pyruvate ferredoxin/flavodoxin oxidoreductase) [pfam:PF01558] and the 4Fe-4S binding domain Fer4 [pfam:PF00037]. It contains a characteristic EKR sequence motif. The exact function of this domain is not known.

This domain of about 280 residues is found in eukaryotes. There are two conserved sequence motifs: GFC and GLL. This family is also known as UPF0704. This domain is found FAP206 [swissprot:Q23H79], a protein associated with cilia and flagella. In the ciliate Tetrahymena, the cilium has radial spokes, each of which is a macromolecular complex essential for motility. A triplet of three radial spokes, RS1, RS2, and RS3, is repeated every 96 nm along the doublet microtubule. Each spoke has a distinct base that docks to the doublet and is linked to different inner dynein arms. Knockout of the FAP206 gene results in slow cell motility and the 96-nm repeats lack RS2 and dynein c. FAP206 is probably part of the front prong and docks RS2 and dynein c to the microtubule [[cite:PUB00082324]].
This is a family of uncharacterised Clostridiales proteins.
The PGG domain is named for the highly conserved sequence motif found at the startt of the domain. The function is not known.

Members of this family carry two distinct, highly conserved sequence motifs, CPPPLYYTHL and HPHLAWLY. The family is found in eukaryotes, and the function is not known. This family lies at the C-terminus of members.
YdiH is a family of proteins found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 62 and 80 amino acids in length. The function is not known.
This family around 100 residues locates in the C-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides, Prevotella and Prevotella species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This domain is found in Rhamnogalacturonan lyase from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron ([swissprot:Q8AAW3]) and other bacterial proteins. It shows an alpha/beta structure [[cite:PUB00100662]] and locates C-terminal to [pfam:PF07944]. The specific function of this domain is still unknown.
This family around 150 residues locates in the C-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Prevotella species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This family around 200 residues locates in the N-terminal of some uncharacterised proteins in various Bacteroides and Alistipes species. The function of this family remains unknown. The N-terminus of this model has been clipped by ~30 residues as it was capturing parts of collagen sequences, [pfam:PF01391].

This family around 100 residues locates in the N-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins and glucuronyl hydrolases in various Bacteroides species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This domain of around 100 residues locates at the C-terminal of some glycerophosphoryl diester phosphodiesterases and uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Prevotella species. The function of this domain is not yet clear, however, it is described as a putative glycerophosphoryl diester phosphodiesterase (PDBe:3i10).
