This entry represents the NTF2-like domain found in the functionally uncharacterised YchJ family protein from Psychrobacter arcticus and related proteins. This domain is usually found flanked by either ([pfam:PF21612]) and ([pfam:PF02810]) at the N and C terminus or flanked on both sides by ([pfam:PF02810]]). The structure of YchJ shows that this domain adopts structure typical for Nuclear transport factor 2 (NTF2) that consists of a curved three-stranded beta-sheet and array of alpha-helices packed on one side of it. The function of this domain is unknown.

Pfam_Description: YchJ family protein, N-terminal zinc binding domain
Pfam_name: YchJ family protein, N-terminal zinc binding domain
Pfam_description: This domain is found at the N-terminal end of the functionally uncharacterised YchJ family protein from Psychrobacter arcticus ([swissprot:Q4FPZ7]) and related proteins from Psychrobacter species. The structure of YchJ shows that this domain folds mainly into an alpha-helical structure. This domain contains the same type of C4 zinc finger as seen in SEC-C motif ([pfam:PF02810]) located at the C terminus of YchJ which suggests a possible internal duplication in the YchJ family.

The majority of proteins in this family consist of a single copy of this domain, though it is also found as a repeat ([swissprot:Q9AJZ7]). A strongly conserved histidine and a aspartate suggest that the domain has an enzymatic function. This family also now includes the family formerly known as the DGPF domain (COG3795). Although its function is unknown it is found fused to a sigma-70 factor family domain in [swissprot:Q9A8M4]. Suggesting that this domain plays a role in transcription initiation (Bateman A per. obs.). This domain is named after the most conserved motif in the alignment.
This protein family includes YciZ from Escherichia coli and similar short sequences encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs) from gammaproteobacteria [[cite:PUB00106067]].

The YcxB-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YcxB protein [swissprot:Q08793], which is a functionally uncharacterised transmembrane protein. This family of proteins is found in bacteria, and is approximately 60 amino acids in length.

YdaS is a transcription factor found in the cryptic prophage Rac of E. coli K12 and represents a novel family within the HigA superfamily as it is distantly related to HigA antitoxins. YdaS can act as a toxin whose expression is regulated by RacR and behaves as a monomer in solution [[cite:PUB00099918],[cite:PUB00099919]]. Previously, it was thought to be an antitoxin that neutralises the toxin YdaT [[cite:PUB00099919]].

YdaT_toxin was first thought to be neutralised by the putative antitoxin YdaS ([pfam:PF15943]) [[cite:PUB00075651]] but recent studies showed that both YdaS and YdaT can act independently as toxins and are regulated by RacR [[cite:PUB00099919]].

This entry represents the YdbH protein from E.coli and related proteins. YdbH is one of the six AsmA-like paralogues in E.coli (YhdP, TamB, YdbH, AsmA, YicH, and YhjG) that have a variable size but share similar predicted structure. In-depth functional characterisation of AsmA-like proteins revealed that YdbH together with the other largest paralogs (YhdP and TamB) are redundant in performing a function that is essential for growth and OM lipid homeostasis in E. coli [[cite:PUB00104645],[cite:PUB00106658]]. Current model based on these analyses suggests that TamA-TamB, YhdP, and YdbH form bridge-like structures that mediate the diffusional flow of phospholipids between the IM and OM [[cite:PUB00104645],[cite:PUB00106658],[cite:PUB00155411]].

Pfam_Description: Mitochondrial resolvase Ydc2 / RNA splicing MRS1
Pfam_name: Mitochondrial resolvase Ydc2 / RNA splicing MRS1
Pfam_description: Members of this family adopt a secondary structure consisting of two beta sheets and one alpha helix, arranged as a beta-alpha-beta motif. Each beta sheet has five strands, arranged in a 32145 order, with the second strand being antiparallel to the rest. Mitochondrial resolvase Ydc2 is capable of resolving Holliday junctions and cleaves DNA after 5'-CT-3' and 5'-TT-3' sequences [[cite:PUB00026683]]. This family also contains the mitochondrial RNA-splicing protein MRS1 which is involved in the excision of group I introns [[cite:PUB00055561],[cite:PUB00055559]].

This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 70 amino acids in length. There is a conserved YDRNRN sequence motif. The E. coli protein has been shown to bind selenium [[cite:PUB00057301]]. This protein shows structural similarity to the KOW motif.

This presumed domain is found in a wide variety of bacterial cell surface proteins. This domain has a highly conserved YDG motif near its N-terminus. This domain is likely related to the [pfam:PF17883] domain.

This domain is found in several Enterobacterial proteins of around 90 residues in length, including E. coli YdgH, YhcN, BhsA and McbA, which play a role in stress response, biofilm formation and pathogenesis [[cite:PUB00097758],[cite:PUB00097759]]. BhsA (also known as ComC) reduces the permeability of the outer membrane to copper and may decrease biofilm formation by repressing cell-cell interaction and cell surface interaction [[cite:PUB00097760]]. Members of this entry have one copy of this domain with the exception of YdgH, which has three copies. The function of this domain is unknown, however, it is suggested to be directly involved in host-pathogen interaction [[cite:PUB00097759]].

This protein family includes Protein YdgV from Escherichia coli and similar sequences from gammaproteobacteria. YdgV is a 33-residues micropeptide encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF). Proteins 50 or fewer residues-long have been shown to regulate the functions of larger proteins in a variety of organisms [[cite:PUB00105763]].

ydhR is a homodimeric protein that comprises of a central four-stranded beta sheet and four surrounding alpha helices [[cite:PUB00035490]]. It shows structural homology to the ActVA-Orf6 and YgiN proteins which indicates it could be a mono-oxygenase.

This family catalyses the synthesis of thymidine monophosphate (dTMP) from deoxyuridine monophosphate (dUMP). The physiological co-substrate has not yet been identified. Previous designation of this famliy as being thymidylate synthase from one paper, [cite:PUB00075419], has been shown to be erroneous [[cite:PUB00057368]]. The proteins are uncharacterised.

EKR is a short, 33 residue, domain found in bacterial and some lower eukaryotic species which lies between a POR (pyruvate ferredoxin/flavodoxin oxidoreductase) [pfam:PF01558] and the 4Fe-4S binding domain Fer4 [pfam:PF00037]. It contains a characteristic EKR sequence motif. The exact function of this domain is not known.

This domain of about 280 residues is found in eukaryotes. There are two conserved sequence motifs: GFC and GLL. This family is also known as UPF0704. This domain is found FAP206 [swissprot:Q23H79], a protein associated with cilia and flagella. In the ciliate Tetrahymena, the cilium has radial spokes, each of which is a macromolecular complex essential for motility. A triplet of three radial spokes, RS1, RS2, and RS3, is repeated every 96 nm along the doublet microtubule. Each spoke has a distinct base that docks to the doublet and is linked to different inner dynein arms. Knockout of the FAP206 gene results in slow cell motility and the 96-nm repeats lack RS2 and dynein c. FAP206 is probably part of the front prong and docks RS2 and dynein c to the microtubule [[cite:PUB00082324]].
This is a family of uncharacterised Clostridiales proteins.
The PGG domain is named for the highly conserved sequence motif found at the startt of the domain. The function is not known.

Members of this family carry two distinct, highly conserved sequence motifs, CPPPLYYTHL and HPHLAWLY. The family is found in eukaryotes, and the function is not known. This family lies at the C-terminus of members.
YdiH is a family of proteins found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 62 and 80 amino acids in length. The function is not known.
This family around 100 residues locates in the C-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides, Prevotella and Prevotella species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This domain is found in Rhamnogalacturonan lyase from Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron ([swissprot:Q8AAW3]) and other bacterial proteins. It shows an alpha/beta structure [[cite:PUB00100662]] and locates C-terminal to [pfam:PF07944]. The specific function of this domain is still unknown.
This family around 150 residues locates in the C-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Prevotella species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This family around 200 residues locates in the N-terminal of some uncharacterised proteins in various Bacteroides and Alistipes species. The function of this family remains unknown. The N-terminus of this model has been clipped by ~30 residues as it was capturing parts of collagen sequences, [pfam:PF01391].
This family around 150 residues locates in the N-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Prevotella species. The function of this family remains unknown.
This family around 100 residues locates in the N-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins and glucuronyl hydrolases in various Bacteroides species. The function of this family remains unknown.

This domain of around 100 residues locates at the C-terminal of some glycerophosphoryl diester phosphodiesterases and uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Prevotella species. The function of this domain is not yet clear, however, it is described as a putative glycerophosphoryl diester phosphodiesterase (PDBe:3i10).
This family around 75 residues locates in the N-terminal of F5/8 type C domain proteins and some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides species. The function of this family remains unknown.
This family around 200 residues locates in the C-terminal of some uncharacterized proteins in various Bacteroides and Parabacteroides species. The function of this family remains unknown.
This is a family of unknown function, however family members such as B277 have been suggested to play a role in viral function [[cite:PUB00046115]].
Family of YdjC-like proteins. This region is possibly involved in the the cleavage of cellobiose-phosphate [[cite:PUB00008633]].

YdjM is a family of putative LexA-binding proteins. Members are predicted to be membrane-bound metal-dependent hydrolases that may be acting as phospholipases. It is a member of the SOS network, that rescues cells from UV and other DNA-damage. Expression of YdjM is regulated by LexA [[cite:PUB00075708],[cite:PUB00155923]].

This family includes the B. subtilis YdjO protein [swissprot:O34759], which is functionally uncharacterised. This is not a homologue of E. coli YdjO, [swissprot:P76210]. B. subtilis YdjO is cold-inducible [[cite:PUB00058235]]. Its expression is induced by the extracytoplasmic function sigma factor sigma-W [[cite:PUB00058236]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length.

This entry includes mitochondrial proteins of unknown function found in yeast. Null mutant showed severe fragmentation of mitochondria and its expression is strongly induced by alpha factor. Members of this entry may have a role in maintenance of mitochondrial morphology [[cite:PUB00101836]]. This entry represents the N-terminal domain which may have an alpha/beta fold.

RNases H are enzymes that specifically hydrolyse RNA when annealed to a complementary DNA and are present in all living organisms. In yeast RNase H2 is composed of a complex of three proteins (Rnh2Ap, Ydr279p and Ylr154p), this family represents the homologues of Ydr279p [[cite:PUB00044465]]. It is not known whether non yeast proteins in this family fulfil the same function. This domain corresponds to the N-terminal triple barrel domain.
Members of this family, which are produced by Williopsis fungi, adopt a secondary structure consisting of eight strands in two beta sheets, in a Greek-key topology [[cite:PUB00035491]].

Metallothioneins are characterised by an abundance of cysteine residues and a lack of generic secondary structure motifs. This protein functions in primary metal storage, transport and detoxification [[cite:PUB00021153]]. For the first 40 residues in the protein the polypeptide wraps around the metal by forming two large parallel loops separated by a deep cleft containing the metal cluster [[cite:PUB00021153]].

We have named this family the YEATS family, after `YNK7', `ENL', `AF-9', and `TFIIF small subunit'. This family also contains the GAS41 protein. All these proteins are thought to have a transcription stimulatory activity

The YebF-like protein family appears to be a group of colicin immunity proteins. As well as YebF the family includes cmi, the colicin M immunity protein [[cite:PUB00053960]]. This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 80 amino acids in length. The alignment contains two conserved cysteine residues that form a disulphide bond in the solved structure [[cite:PUB00057376]].

This family consists of several bacterial YebG proteins of around 75 residues in length. The exact function of this protein is unknown but it is thought to be involved in the SOS response. The induction of the yebG gene occurs as cell enter into the stationary growth phase and is dependent on is dependent on cyclic AMP and H-NS [[cite:PUB00013010]].
This short protein is uncharacterized. It seems likely to be of phage origin as it is found in [swissprot:Q9MCU2] and [swissprot:Q9MCS4]. The protein is also found in a variety of enteric bacteria.

Pfam_Description: Ribosomal RNA small subunit methyltransferase F, pre-PUA domain
Pfam_name: Ribosomal RNA small subunit methyltransferase F, pre-PUA domain
Pfam_description: This domain is found in Ribosomal RNA small subunit methyltransferase F from Escherichia coli (YebU) and similar proteins mainly from proteobacteria. YebU requires S-adenosyl-l-methionine (SAM) to specifically methylate the cytosine at position 1407 of assembled 30 S rRNA subunits. This proteins is organized into two distinct structural domains: the N-terminal MTase domain (catalytic domain), which can be divided in [pfam:PF17125] and [pfam:PF01189], and the C-terminal, also consisting of two subdomains. This entry represents the first of these subdomains, which is found N-terminal to the PUA- like domain ([pfam:PF13636]). The pre-PUA domain has six beta-strands that form a central sheet in an anti-parallel fashion, and three alpha-helices packing against the edges of the sheet [[cite:PUB00036064]].
This family consists of several bacterial YecM proteins of unknown function.

The YecR-like family of lipoproteins includes the YecR protein from E. coli [swissprot:P76308]. This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length.

This family of proteins related to the YedD protein is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 140 amino acids in length. These proteins are lipoproteins.

Pfam_Description: YegS C-terminal NAD kinase beta sandwich-like domain
Pfam_name: YegS C-terminal NAD kinase beta sandwich-like domain
Pfam_description: This entry represents the C-terminal domain found in the YegS protein [[cite:PUB00039707],[cite:PUB00048593]]. It is related to the beta sandwich domain of NAD kinases. The structure of YegS reveals a two-domain protein with the active site crevice found between the two domains. The C-terminal domain contains 13 beta-strands and two alpha-helices. The likely substrate for YegS is phosphatidylglycerol [[cite:PUB00039707]].

The YejG protein family is a group of functionally uncharacterised proteins related to [swissprot:P0AD21]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length.

The YesK-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YesK protein [swissprot:O31514], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is regulated by the sporulation-specific sigma factor sigma-E [[cite:PUB00057341]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length.
This entry represents the N-terminal region of the YetF protein which is composed of three transmembrane helices.

This protein family includes the immunity protein YezG from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences predominantly found in Firmicutes. YezG is the antitoxin component of a LXG toxin-antitoxin (TA) module that promote kin selection, mediate competition in biofilms, and drive spatial segregation of different strains, probably helping to avoid warfare between strains in biofilms [[cite:PUB00101092]]. It shows an alpha/beta structure with an antiparallel beta-sheet.
This family contains the precursor of the bacterial protein YfaZ (approximately 180 residues long). Many members of this family are hypothetical proteins.

This domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain represents the C-terminal of the uncharacterized protein YfbK. This domain is about 180 amino acids in length. This domain is found at the C-terminal of [pfam:PF00092].

This presumed domain is about 160 residues long. It is found in archaebacteria and eubacteria. In [swissprot:Q9EUM2] it is associated with a helix-turn-helix domain. This suggests that this may be a ligand binding domain.
This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. THey are related to the short YfcL protein from E. coli.
YfdX is a protein found in Proteobacteria of unknown function. The protein coding for this gene is regulated by EvgA in E. coli [[cite:PUB00053495]].

This family consists of a group of proteins predominantly found in Enterobacteria, including Uncharacterized protein YfeC from Escherichia coli, a dual transcriptional regulator predicted to form homodimers [[cite:PUB00101945]].

The YfhD-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YfhD protein [swissprot:O31572], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is regulated by the sporulation-specific sigma factor sigma-F [[cite:PUB00034417]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 50 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue E that may be functionally important.

The YfhE-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YfhE protein [swissprot:O31573], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression may be regulated by the sigma factor sigma-B, which regulates the expression of stress-response proteins [[cite:PUB00057342]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 40 amino acids in length. There is a conserved QEV sequence motif.

This protein is a conserved membrane protein [[cite:PUB00044549]]. The yfhO gene is transcribed in Difco sporulation medium and the transcription is affected by the YvrGHb two-component system. Some members of this family have been annotated as glycosyl transferases of the PMT family.

This outer membrane lipoprotein carries a TPR-like region towards its N-terminal. YfiO in E.coli is one of three outer membrane lipoproteins that form a multicomponent YaeT complex in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria that is involved in the targeting and folding of beta-barrel outer membrane proteins. YfiO is the only essential lipoprotein component of the complex. It is required for the proper assembly and/or targeting of outer membrane proteins to the outer membrane. Through its interactions with NlpB it maintains the functional integrity of the YaeT complex.
This entry is based on the E. coli YfjS and YafY lipoproteins.
This protein is adjacent to YfkA in B. subtilis. In other bacterial species it is fused to this protein. As YfkA contains a Radical SAM domain it suggests this domain is interacts with them.

The YfkD-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YfkD protein [swissprot:O34579], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is regulated by the sigma factor sigma-B, which regulates the expression of stress-response proteins, and by the forespore-specific sigma factor sigma-G [[cite:PUB00034417],[cite:PUB00057363]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 254 and 265 amino acids in length.

Pfam_Description: Heat induced stress protein YflT domain
Pfam_name: Heat induced stress protein YflT domain
Pfam_description: YflT is a heat induced protein. According to AlphaFold this domain is composed of a core of four beta strands that form a central beta sheet with alpha helices packed on both side. This family shows sequence similarity to [pfam:PF11821] which includes the ActD protein which forms an accessory component of the Alternative complex III which catalyses the oxidation of membrane-bound quinol and the reduction of cytochrome c or an equivalent electron carrier. This suggests that members of this family may also be involved in forming larger redox complexes.

Pfam_Description: Uncharacterised protein from bacillus cereus group
Pfam_name: Uncharacterised protein from bacillus cereus group
Pfam_description: This family is conserved in the Bacillus cereus group. Several members are called YfmQ but the function is not known.

The YfzA-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YfzA protein [swissprot:C0H3X6] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length.

The YgaB-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YgaB protein [swissprot:P71080], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length.

Pfam_Description: Inner membrane protein YgaP-like, transmembrane domain
Pfam_name: Inner membrane protein YgaP-like, transmembrane domain
Pfam_description: This domain is found in proteins from bacteria and archaea, including Inner membrane protein YgaP from Escherichia coli, a membrane protein with a rhodanese domain (Pfam: PF00581) that may have sulfurtransferase activity. YgaP adopts a dimeric assembly. This entry represents the transmembrane domain. It consist of two slightly tilted alpha-helices [[cite:PUB00100968]]. Structure prediction suggests that this region may homodimerise to form a 4 helical bundle.
The function of ygaB is not known but it is a promoter that is stimulated by the presence of nitrous oxide [[cite:PUB00033788]]. It is regulated by the gene-product of the bacterial nsrR gene.
The ygbB protein is a putative enzyme of deoxy-xylulose pathway (terpenoid biosynthesis) [[cite:PUB00007261]].

YgfZ is a folate-binding protein involved in regulating the level of ATP-dnaA and in the modification of some tRNAs [[cite:PUB00022265],[cite:PUB00043084]]. It consists of a folate-binding domain at the N-terminal ([pfam:PF01571]) and a six-stranded antiparallel beta-barrel at the C-terminal, represented in this entry, with identical topology found at the C-terminal of elongation factors Tu and eEF-1alpha and in the gamma subunit of the initiation factor eIF2 [[cite:PUB00022265]].

This family represents bacterial proteins predominantly found in Gammaproteobacteria. YggL from E.coli has been characterised and it interacts with ribosome subunits 50S and 70S. It is a 50S-binding protein likely to be involved in particle assembly. It is a small protein extremely conserved in Gammaproteobacteria but also present in orders Burkholderiales and Neisseriales from Betaproteobacteria [[cite:PUB00095181]].

This family includes subunit CCB3 of cofactor assembly complex C, involved in c-type cytochrome maturation in photosynthetic organisms [[cite:PUB00075315]]. This family also includes uncharacterised protein YggT, associated with bacteria outside the cyanobacteria.

This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Glucosidase YgjK from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial enzymes from the glycoside hydrolase family 63 (GH63) from bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes. YgjK is organised into N- and A- domains and a linker between them. This entry includes the N-domain and the linker. The N-domain is composed of 18 antiparallel beta-strands divided into two beta- sheets and is classified as a super-beta-sandwich. The linker is composed of two helices and produces a significant curvature between the two domains [[cite:PUB00050905],[cite:PUB00151961],[cite:PUB00151962]].

This is a conserved domain containing the catalytic zinc-metallopeptidase (HExxH) catalytic motif. Proteins containing this domain are found in some archaebacteria, as well as Helicobacter pylori. The proteins are 190-240 amino acids long, with the C terminus being the most conserved region, containing three conserved histidines [[cite:PUB00098014],[cite:PUB00098016],[cite:PUB00098015],[cite:PUB00084997]]. This domain is found in YgjP from E. coli [[cite:PUB00084997]], a predicted metal-dependent hydrolase that hydrolyses UTP to UMP and diphosphate in vitro; and in MJ0123 from Methanocaldococcus jannaschii (also referred to as projannalysin) [[cite:PUB00098015]].

Pfam_Description: Obg-like GTPase YGR210-like, G4 motif-containing domain
Pfam_name: Obg-like GTPase YGR210-like, G4 motif-containing domain
Pfam_description: This domain is part of the G domain found at the C-terminus of [pfam:PF01926] in archaeal and eukaryotic GTP-binding proteins. Members of this entry form a subfamily within the Obg family of GTPases and includes YGR210 from yeasts and its homologues from archaea [[cite:PUB00036769]]. This domain seems to be necessary for the complete activity of the protein for binding of both adenine and guanine nucleotides, with a preference for guanine nucleotides. This domain contains the NKxD motif, known as the G4 motif [[cite:PUB00036769]].
This entry represents the substrate binding domain of YgxA from Bacillus subtilis and similar sequences.

This domain can be found in uncharacterised proteins in viruses, archaea and bacteria, most notably it is found in YhcG proteins found in E.coli. This entry represents the C-terminal PDDEXK domain belonging to the PD-(D/E)XK superfamily of nucleases involved in DNA recombination and repair [[cite:PUB00091061]]. Profile HMM analysis identified a relationship between this C-terminal domain of YhcG and [pfam:PF01939] , a family of NucS endonucleases [[cite:PUB00054003]]. YHcG was identified in association with DNA processing enzymes, including the restriction complexes HsdMRS and McrABC, the integrases IntF and IntS, and the recombinase PinE [[cite:PUB00091061]].

The YhdB-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YhdB protein [swissprot:O07530], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 57 and 82 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: LMVRT and FLHAY.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.

This family includes proteins that are mainly from Firmicutes and Proteobacteria. Family members bear the consensus signature of 'EExxR' the second motif 'HxxxE' and the third motif 'H/Qxxxs'. The fourth motif, 'HxxxB', is shared by the PrsW proteases [pfam:PF13367] and the CPBP [pfam:PF02517], and APH-1 families. There are currently no experimental functional data for members of this group, however, they are predicted to be integral membrane proteins with several transmembrane segments and hypothesized metalloprotease function. YhfC intramembrane metalloprotease, CPBP family (type II CAAX Proteases and Bacteriocin Processing enzymes), PrsW proteases and APH-1 are distantly related. They share four predicted core transmembrane segments and possess similar, yet distinct sets of sequence motifs [[cite:PUB00091031]].

This protein family includes proteins predominantly found in Gammaproteobacteria, such as YhfG from Escherichia coli. YhfG is a FicA antitoxin homologue (also known as antitoxin EcFicA) that interacts with EcFiT and forms a complex with it. YhfG shows a unique conformation, forming two parallel alpha- helices linked by a 10-residues loop. The structure of the complex shows a highly conserved extended ligand-binding pocket [[cite:PUB00100669]].

The YhfH-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YhfH protein [swissprot:O07606], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is repressed by the Spx paralogue MgsR, which regulates genes involved in stress response [[cite:PUB00057340]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 42 and 53 amino acids in length.
This entry represents the C-terminal domain of the uncharacterised protein YhfS from E.coli and similar sequences. This is an alpha/beta domain commonly found in PLP-dependent enzymes.
This family represents a conserved region in a number of uncharacterised plant proteins.

This family is conserved in Firmicutes and Proteobacteria. The function is not known but several members are annotated as being homologues of E coli YhfT, a protein thought to be involved in fatty acid oxidation.

This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 110 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF08874]. There are two completely conserved residues (D and R) that may be functionally important.

This domain family is found in bacteria and eukaryotes, and is approximately 30 amino acids in length. There is a conserved WMPC sequence motif. There are two completely conserved residues (A and C) that may be functionally important.
This is a family of eukaryotic proteins. Most members carry a highly distinctive, conserved sequence motif of FWWh, where h represents a hydrophobic residue. The function of the family is not known.

This domain is found at the C-terminal end of a group of bacterial proteins, including Uncharacterized protein YhfX from Escherichia coli, which may be related to DNA recombination. The function of this domain is still unknown. It is often found associated to [pfam:PF01168].
This domain is often found in association with the helix-turn-helix domain HTH_41 ([pfam:PF14502]). It includes YhfZ proteins from Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri.

The members of this family are similar to the hypothetical protein yhhN expressed by E. coli ([swissprot:P37616]). Many are annotated as possible transmembrane proteins, and in fact they all have a high proportion of hydrophobic residues. A human member of this family, formerly known as TMEM86B, is a lysoplasmalogenase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of the vinyl ether bond of lysoplasmalogen[[cite:PUB00081209]]. Putative conserved active site residues have been proposed for the YhhN family [[cite:PUB00081210]].

This short presumed domain is about 50 amino acid residues long. It often contains two cysteines that may be functionally important. This domain is found in copper transporting ATPases, some phenol hydroxylases and in a set of uncharacterised membrane proteins including [swissprot:Q9CNI0]. This domain is named after three of the most conserved amino acids it contains. The domain may be metal binding, possibly copper ions. This domain is duplicated in some copper transporting ATPases.
This domain family is found in bacteria, eukaryotes and viruses, and is typically between 141 and 198 amino acids in length. There is a conserved YHYH sequence motif.

The YhzD-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YhzD protein [swissprot:C0H3Y1] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length. There is a conserved GKL sequence motif.
This domain consists of two transmembrane helices and a conserved linking section.

The sequences featured in this family are similar to two proteins expressed by Lactococcus lactis, YibE ([swissprot:Q9CHC5]) and YibF ([swissprot:Q9CHC4]). Most of the members of this family are annotated as being putative membrane proteins, and in fact the sequences contain a high proportion of hydrophobic residues.

This domain is found at the C-terminal end of Endoribonuclease YicC from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial sequences. YicC, which is important for cells in the stationary phase, and essential for growth at high temperatures [[cite:PUB00020576]], contributes to degradation of the small RNA (sRNA) RhyB via collaboration with the exoribonuclease PNPase [[cite:PUB00151089]] and seems to generate a 3'-OH and a 5'-phosphate group [[cite:PUB00151088]].

This domain is found at the N-terminal end of Endoribonuclease YicC from Escherichia coli and similar bacterial sequences. YicC, which is important for cells in the stationary phase, and essential for growth at high temperatures [[cite:PUB00020576]], contributes to degradation of the small RNA (sRNA) RhyB via collaboration with the exoribonuclease PNPase [[cite:PUB00151089]] and seems to generate a 3'-OH and a 5'-phosphate group [[cite:PUB00151088]].
This entry includes the uncharacterised protein YidB from E. coli [swissprot:P09996]. This entry was previously a subset of the DUF937 family.
This is the periplasmic domain of YidC, a bacterial membrane protein which is required for the insertion and assembly of inner membrane proteins [[cite:PUB00050750],[cite:PUB00050682]].

Pfam_Description: Putative membrane protein insertion efficiency factor
Pfam_name: Putative membrane protein insertion efficiency factor
Pfam_description: This family consists of membrane insertion efficiency factor proteins. They contain three conserved cysteine residues. Family members such as YidD may be involved in insertion of integral membrane proteins into the membrane by assisting YidC (membrane protein insertase). Some members of the yidD family have been previously thought to posses alpha-hemolysin activity, however no sufficient evidence was found to corroborate this idea. Secondary structure prediction indicated the presence of three alpha-helices in YidD. None of the three alpha-helices appeared sufficiently hydrophobic to serve as a transmembrane, suggesting a cytoplasmic localization for YidD. However, a closer examination of the alpha-helical wheel projection of the predicted first alpha-helix in YidD suggested an amphipathic structure in its N-terminal region which might be involved in membrane targeting [[cite:PUB00064882]].

This family includes the B. subtilis YphB protein [swissprot:P50742], which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is regulated by the sporulation transcription factor sigma-F, however it is not essential for sporulation or germination [[cite:PUB00058237]]. This is not a homologue of E. coli YphB, which belongs to [pfam:PF01263]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 276 and 300 amino acids in length and contain a conserved YIEGIA motif. Structure predictions show that these proteins contain an N-terminal transmembrane domain composed of five alpha helices. This domain is followed by a C-terminal domain that is likely cytosolic. Structure prediction shows that this family likely forms a homohexameric structure. Structure prediction also shows that this complex is capped by a homohexamer of proteins belonging to [pfam:PF21835] (pers. observation A Bateman).

This entry contains a family of small protein of unknown function. Proteins in this family are found in Firmicutes. These proteins adopt a beta sheet structure with four strands with an alpha helix packed on one face between the second and third strands. Using AlphaFold we can identify a likely hexameric ring complex. Additionally these proteins likely form a cap on a goblet like hexameric complex of [pfam:PF14045]. Analysis of genomic context suggests this larger complex is involved in spore germination and possibly phospholipid synthesis or regulation (pers.obs. Alex Bateman).

YIF1 (Yip1 interacting factor) is an integral membrane protein that is required for membrane fusion of ER derived vesicles [[cite:PUB00045173]]. It also plays a role in the biogenesis of ER derived COPII transport vesicles [[cite:PUB00033378]].

YihI activates the GTPase activity of Der, a 50S ribosomal subunit stability factor [[cite:PUB00053968]]. The stimulation is specific to Der as YihI does not stimulate the GTPase activity of Era or ObgE. The interaction of YihI with Der requires only the C-terminal 78 amino acids of YihI [[cite:PUB00053968]]. A yihI deletion mutant is viable and shows a shorter lag period, but the same post-lag growth rate as a wild-type strain. yihI is expressed during the lag period. Overexpression of yihI inhibits cell growth and biogenesis of the 50S ribosomal subunit [[cite:PUB00053968]]. YihI is an unusual, highly hydrophilic protein with an uneven distribution of charged residues, resulting in an N-terminal region with high pI and a C-terminal region with low pI [[cite:PUB00053968]].

This entry consists of a broadly distributed uncharacterised domain often found as a standalone protein. The member from Shewanella oneidensis is described from crystallography work as a putative thioesterase because it belongs to the HotDog clan of enzymes. About half of the members of this family are fused to an Acetyltransf_1 domain [pfam:PF00583].

This small triple helical domain has been predicted to assume a topology similar to helix-turn-helix domains. These domains are found at the C-terminus of proteins related to [swissprot:P32157] [[cite:PUB00019067],[cite:PUB00100687]].

The Yip1 integral membrane domain contains four transmembrane alpha helices. The domain is characterised by the motifs DLYGP and GY. The Yip1 protein is a golgi protein involved in vesicular transport that interacts with GTPases [[cite:PUB00020577]].

This family includes both Yippee-type proteins and Mis18 kinetochore proteins. Yippee are putative zinc-binding/DNA-binding proteins. Mis18 are proteins involved in the priming of centromeres for recruiting CENP-A. Mis18-alpha and beta form part of a small complex with Mis18-binding protein. Mis18-alpha is found to interact with DNA de-methylases through a Leu-rich region located at its carboxyl terminus [[cite:PUB00066712]]. This entry also includes the CULT domain proteins such as Cereblon [[cite:PUB00078711]].

Pfam_Description: Uncharacterised 5xTM membrane BCR, YitT family COG1284
Pfam_name: Uncharacterised 5xTM membrane BCR, YitT family COG1284
Pfam_description: This is probably a bacterial ABC transporter permease (personal obs:Yeats C).

YjbE is part of a four gene operon which is involved in exopolysaccharide production. The expression of YjbE is higher than the rest of the operon yjbEFGH. It appears to be restricted to Enterobacteriaceae [[cite:PUB00058168]]. YbjE is one of four gene-products expressed from an operon, yjbEFGH, which is regulated by the Rcs phosphorelay in a RcsA-dependent manner, similar to that of other exopolysaccharide biosynthetic pathways. It is highly possible that the yjbEFGH operon encodes a system involved in EPS secretion since none of the products is predicted to have enzymic activity, the products are all secreted and YbjH and F are predicted to be beta-barrel lipoproteins similar to porins. It may be that the operon products play some role in biofilm formation and/or matrix production [[cite:PUB00058168]].

Pfam_Description: Group 4 capsule polysaccharide lipoprotein gfcB, YjbF
Pfam_name: Group 4 capsule polysaccharide lipoprotein gfcB, YjbF
Pfam_description: This family includes lipoprotein GfcB (YmcC), involved in group 4 capsule polysaccharide formation [[cite:PUB00066719]]. YjbF is a family of Gram-negative bacterial outer-membrane lipoproteins, predicted to be a beta-barrel and possibly a porin that is one of four gene-products expressed from an operon, yjbEFGH, which is regulated by the Rcs phosphorelay in a RcsA-dependent manner, similar to that of other exopolysaccharide biosynthetic pathways. It is highly possible that the yjbEFGH operon encodes a system involved in EPS secretion since none of the products is predicted to have enzymic activity, the products are all secreted and YbjF and H are predicted to be beta-barrel lipoproteins similar to porins. It may be that the operon products play some role in biofilm formation and/or matrix production [[cite:PUB00066719]].

YjbH is a family of Gram-negative beta-barrel outer-membrane lipoproteins that act as putative porins. YbjH is one of four gene-products expressed from an operon, yjbEFGH, which is regulated by the Rcs phosphorelay in a RcsA-dependent manner, similar to that of other exopolysaccharide biosynthetic pathways. It is highly possible that the yjbEFGH operon encodes a system involved in EPS secretion since none of the products is predicted to have enzymic activity, the products are all secreted and YbjH and F are predicted to be beta-barrel lipoproteins similar to porins. It may be that the operon products play some role in biofilm formation and/or matrix production [[cite:PUB00058168]].
YjbR has a CyaY-like fold [[cite:PUB00066658]].
Ycf90 is an algal protein located in chloroplasts. Its function is unknown.
This is a family of bacterial proteins. The function is unknown.

This is a family of unknown function. However, family members such as yjcZ has been shown to be sporulation specific and transcribed by the SigK RNA polymerase beginning at t4 of sporulation [[cite:PUB00058247]].
Function of this protein family is not known.
This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacilli.

This domain family is found in VraX proteins from Staphylococcus aureus. The vraX gene belongs to the vra operon together with the vraA gene encoding for a long chain fatty acid-CoA ligase, which is up-regulated in the VISA (vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus) [[cite:PUB00085343]]. The gene product, a 55-amino acids protein,is upregulated in the stress response to cell wall-active antibiotics and other surface-interactive molecules. VraX harbors a putative phosphorylation site, and could therefore be involved in regulatory processes within the cell. However, no exact function has been demonstrated [[cite:PUB00085344]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteria phage P22 and Enterobacteria phage lambda.
This is a family of unknown function found in Yersinia pestis.
This is a family of unknown function found in beta-herpesvirus. Family members such as UL124 is a predicted membrane glycoprotein with one predicted trans-membrane region [[cite:PUB00085213]].
Family members found in alphabaculoviruses such as orf45 have been implicated in late gene expression when linked to orf41 [[cite:PUB00085207]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Cytomegalovirus. One of the family members US30 is a putative membrane glycoprotein with one predicted trans-membrane region.

YjcQ is a protein of approx. 100 residues containing four alpha helices and three beta strands. It is expressed in bacteria and also in viruses. It appears to be under the regulation of SigD RNA polymerase which is responsible for the expression of many genes encoding cell-surface proteins related to flagellar assembly, motility, chemotaxis and autolysis in the late exponential growth phase. The exact function of YjcQ is unknown [[cite:PUB00044550]]. However, it is thought to be a prophage head protein in viruses [[cite:PUB00044231]].

This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. The family includes the YjcZ protein from E. coli [swissprot:P39267]. This family of proteins is found in enteric bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 300 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: FGD and MPR.

This is a family of unknown function. However, family members such as yjcZ has been shown to be sporulation specific and transcribed by the SigK RNA polymerase beginning at t4 of sporulation [[cite:PUB00058247]].
Function of this protein family is not known.
This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacilli.

This domain family is found in VraX proteins from Staphylococcus aureus. The vraX gene belongs to the vra operon together with the vraA gene encoding for a long chain fatty acid-CoA ligase, which is up-regulated in the VISA (vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus) [[cite:PUB00085343]]. The gene product, a 55-amino acids protein,is upregulated in the stress response to cell wall-active antibiotics and other surface-interactive molecules. VraX harbors a putative phosphorylation site, and could therefore be involved in regulatory processes within the cell. However, no exact function has been demonstrated [[cite:PUB00085344]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteria phage P22 and Enterobacteria phage lambda.
This is a family of unknown function found in Yersinia pestis.
This is a family of unknown function found in beta-herpesvirus. Family members such as UL124 is a predicted membrane glycoprotein with one predicted trans-membrane region [[cite:PUB00085213]].
Family members found in alphabaculoviruses such as orf45 have been implicated in late gene expression when linked to orf41 [[cite:PUB00085207]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Cytomegalovirus. One of the family members US30 is a putative membrane glycoprotein with one predicted trans-membrane region.

YjeF-N domain is a novel version of the Rossmann fold with a set of catalytic residues and structural features that are different from the conventional dehydrogenases [[cite:PUB00043768]]. YjeF-N domain is fused to Ribokinases in bacteria (YjeF), where they may be phosphatases, and to divergent Sm and the FDF domain in eukaryotes (Dcp3p and FLJ21128) [[cite:PUB00043768]], where they may be involved in decapping and catalyze hydrolytic RNA-processing reactions [[cite:PUB00043768]].
YjeJ is a family of bacterial proteins. The domains and proteins in this family vary in length from 283 to 284 amino acids. The function is not yet known. All proteins are Gammaproteobacteria.

This family of proteins is regulated in B. subtilis by SigD, and is likely to be involved in motility or flagellin production, Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length, and contain two highly conserved asparagine residues.

YjgF_Endoribonuc is a putative endoribonuclease. The structure is of beta-alpha-beta-alpha-beta(2) domains common both to bacterial chorismate mutase and to members of the YjgF family. These proteins form trimers with a three-fold symmetry with three closely-packed beta-sheets. The YjgF family is a large, widely distributed family of proteins of unknown biochemical function that are highly conserved among eubacteria, archaea and eukaryotes [[cite:PUB00028112]].

Pfam_Description: Putative toxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin pair
Pfam_name: Putative toxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin pair
Pfam_description: YjhX_toxin is a putative toxin of a bacterial toxin-antitoxin pair, which is neutralised by the proteins YjhQ in family [pfam:PF00583].

Members in this family are homologues to enzymes known to undergo activation by a radical SAM protein to create an active site glycyl radical. This family appears to be activated by the YjjW radical SAM protein, usually encoded by an adjacent gene.

This entry represents a domain found in a group of fungal cell wall proteins, including Tos1 and YJL171C from budding yeasts. They contain 5 highly conserved cysteines, two of which form a characteristic CGC sequence motif. Their function is not clear. It has been shown that these proteins are related to known glycosyl hydrolases [[cite:PUB00097737]].
This domain is found in the N-terminal region of cell wall proteins, including Tos1 and YJL171C from budding yeasts. The function of this glycine-rich region is unknown.

The YjzC-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YjzC protein [swissprot:O34585], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length.

This entry represents proteins that are related to the YkoP protein from B. subtilis [swissprot:O34495]. This protein is as yet uncharacterised. AlphaFold prediction shows that is is composed of a single domain. The structure shows similarity to GNAT family acetyltransferases. This domain is sometimes associated with [pfam:PF01522], which is a polysaccharide deacetylase enzyme.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.

This family of proteins are found in a range of bacteria. It has been shown that this domain can act as an L,D-transpeptidase that gives rise to an alternative pathway for peptidoglycan cross-linking [[cite:PUB00038821]]. This gives bacteria resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics that inhibit PBPs which usually carry out the cross-linking reaction. The conserved region contains a conserved histidine and cysteine, with the cysteine thought to be an active site residue. Several members of this family contain peptidoglycan binding domains. The molecular structure of YkuD protein shows this domain has a novel tertiary fold consisting of a beta-sandwich with two mixed sheets, one containing five strands and the other, six strands. The two beta-sheets form a cradle capped by an alpha-helix. This family was formerly called the ErfK/YbiS/YcfS/YnhG family, but is now named after the first protein of known structure.
This family is related to [pfam:PF03734].

This family of proteins are found in a range of bacteria. It has been shown that this domain can act as an L,D-transpeptidase that gives rise to an alternative pathway for peptidoglycan cross-linking [[cite:PUB00038821]]. This gives bacteria resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics that inhibit PBPs which usually carry out the cross-linking reaction. The conserved region contains a conserved histidine and cysteine, with the cysteine thought to be an active site residue. Several members of this family contain peptidoglycan binding domains. The molecular structure of YkuD protein shows this domain has a novel tertiary fold consisting of a beta-sandwich with two mixed sheets, one containing five strands and the other, six strands. The two beta-sheets form a cradle capped by an alpha-helix. This family was formerly called the ErfK/YbiS/YcfS/YnhG family, but is now named after the first protein of known structure.
This family is related to [pfam:PF03734].

In Bacillus species this highly conserved region of the YkuI protein lies immediately downstream of the EAL (diguanylate cyclase/phosphodiesterase domain 2) [pfam:PF00563] domain so that together they form a monomer which dimerises for its enzymatic action. The region contains three alpha helices and five beta strands and is the C-terminal half of the structure.

YkyA is a family of proteins containing a lipoprotein signal and a hydrolase domain. It is similar to cell wall binding proteins and might also be recognisable by a host immune defence system. It is thus likely to belong to pathways important for pathogenicity [[cite:PUB00044551]].

The YkyB-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YkyB protein [swissprot:P42430], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 150 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: NRHAKTA and HLG.
The proteins in this family are designated YL1 [[cite:PUB00017178]]. These proteins have been shown to be DNA-binding and may be a transcription factor [[cite:PUB00017178]].

This domain is found in proteins of the YL1 family [[cite:PUB00017178]]. These proteins have been shown to be DNA-binding and may be a transcription factor [[cite:PUB00017178]]. This domain is found in proteins that are not YL1 proteins.
Members of this family include proteins annotated as inner membrane protein YlaC in E. coli and Salmonella. The function of this family is unknown.

The YlaH-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YlaH protein [swissprot:O07632], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length. There is a conserved LGFA sequence motif.

This is a conserved, three transmembrane helix-containing domain found fused to certain prokaryotic YEATS domain. Genome context displacement patterns predict an effector role for this domain, as a membrane-perforating, cell-suicide response-enacting domain [[cite:PUB00097693]].
This is a family of putative bacterial coat proteins. Proteins in this family are approximately 140 amino acids in length.

The YlbE-like protein family includes the B. subtilis protein YlbE [swissprot:O34958] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of cytosolic proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There is a conserved WYR sequence motif.
This protein family includes Protein YldA from Escherichia coli [[cite:PUB00106067]], a 29-residues long sequence predicted to adopt an alpha-helical configuration.

YLDV-IL18BP is unique among the diverse family of mammalian and poxvirus IL18BPs in that it uses a bivalent binding mode and a unique set of interacting residues for binding IL18 [[cite:PUB00154334]]. YLDV-IL18BP binds to the same surface of IL18 used by other IL18BPs, suggesting that all IL18BPs use a conserved inhibitory mechanism by blocking a putative receptor-binding site on IL18. This domain adopts a typical Ig-like fold.
YliH is induced in biofilms and is involved in repression of motility in the biofilms [[cite:PUB00044175]]. YliH is also known as bssR (regulator of biofilm through signal secreton).
This is a domain found at the N-terminal of the Putative RNA-binding protein YlmH.
This domain adopts an RRM like fold and is found in the B. subtilis YlmH cell division protein.

The YLP motif is found in several drosophila proteins. Its function is unknown, however the presence of completely conserved tyrosine residues and its presence in [swissprot:Q15303] may suggest it could be a substrate for tyrosine kinases.

The structure of a representative of this family has been solved (pdb:4dci) and found to form a tetrameric structure of prefoldin-like architecture with the beta-barrel core and helical coiled coil tentacles. This suggests that this family may act as molecular chaperones.
The YlxR family has been demonstrated to regulate metabolic gene expression [[cite:PUB00101021]].

The YlzJ-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YlzJ protein [swissprot:C0H413], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 61 and 72 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (L and G) that may be functionally important.
This family of proteins contain 6 HXH motifs and is named after the B. subtilis YmaF protein. It seems likely that these are involved in metal binding. The function of this protein is unknown.

Pfam_Description: Putative antitoxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin system
Pfam_name: Putative antitoxin of bacterial toxin-antitoxin system
Pfam_description: YmcE_antitoxin is the putative antitoxin for the supposed bacterial toxin GnsA, UniProtKB:P0AC92, family [pfam:PF08178] [[cite:PUB00075651]].

This protein family includes Protein YmcF from Escherichia coli and similar sequences from gammaproteobacteria. YmcF is a 62-residues long cold shock-regulated micropeptide encoded by an small open reading frame (smORF)[[cite:PUB00155924]].
This family of putative phosphoesterases contains the B. subtilis protein YmdB [swissprot:O31775].

This domain is found at the N-terminal end of a group of proteins predominantly found in fungi, plants and basal metazoans, including Mitochondrial inner membrane i-AAA protease supercomplex subunit YME1 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae. This domain adopts a tetratricopeptide repeat fold [[cite:PUB00151733]].
This family corresponds to subunit 8 (YMF19) of the F0 complex of plant and algae mitochondrial F-ATPases ([ec:3.6.1.34]).
This domain represents the C-terminal region of YMF19 of the F0 complex of mitochondrial F-ATPases from plants [[cite:PUB00016657]]. This family is found in conjunction with [pfam:PF02326].

YmgB is part of the three gene cluster ymgABC which has a role in biofilm development and stability. YmgB represses biofilm formation in rich medium containing glucose, decreases cellular motility and also protects the cell from acid which indicates that YmgB has an important function in acid-resistance [[cite:PUB00048568]]. YmgB binds as a dimer to genes which are important for biofilm formation via a ligand. Due to its important function in acid resistance it is also known as AriR (regulator of acid resistance influenced by indole) [[cite:PUB00048568]].
This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 110 amino acids in length.

This protein family includes Protein YmiA from Escherichia coli and similar sequences found in gammaproteobacteria. YmiA is the 46-residue product of a small open reading frame (smORF) [[cite:PUB00105763]]. Its specific function is unknown.

The YmzC-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YmzC protein [swissprot:O31797], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 58 and 91 amino acids in length. There is a conserved ELR sequence motif.
This protein family includes Protein YnaL from Escherichia coli [[cite:PUB00106067]], a 57-residues long protein encoded by a small open reading frame (smORF).

This entry includes bacterial YNCE proteins which consist of a beta-propeller structure (the so-called YVTN beta-propeller) [[cite:PUB00058438],[cite:PUB00151879]] which binds DNA [[cite:PUB00151879]].

The YndJ-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YndJ protein [swissprot:O31813], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family is found in bacteria and archaea, and is typically between 222 and 269 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved G residues that may be functionally important.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.

The YniB-like protein family includes the E. coli YniB protein [swissprot:P76208] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 180 amino acids in length. This family of proteins are integral membrane proteins.

This family of proteins is predominantly found in Saccharomycetales, including YNR034W-A (also known as Ego4) and YCR075W-A (Ego2) from Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Ego2 is a component of the yeast EGO complex (EGOC), which is responsible for the amino acid-dependent activation of the target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1). Ego2 adopts a Roadblock domain fold that consists of a central core beta-sheet of five anti-parallel beta-strands flanked by a long alpha-helix on the bottom side. Ego4 shows a similar configuration. It interacts with the GTPase Gtr2, but its specific function remains unknown [[cite:PUB00100978],[cite:PUB00100979]].

This protein family includes Protein YoaL from Escherichia coli, the product of a small open reading frame (smORF), which may serve a regulatory role in the expression of its downstream gene [[cite:PUB00105763]].

The YoaP-like domain is found at the C-terminus of the B. subtilis YoaP protein [swissprot:O34983]. It is found in bacteria and archaea, and is approximately 40 amino acids in length. The family is found in association with [pfam:PF00583]. There is a single completely conserved residue A that may be functionally important.

The YobH-like protein family includes the YobH protein from E. coli [swissprot:Q2MB16] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: GYG and GLGL.
This is a P-loop NTPase involved in antiviral immunity in bacteria. Members of this entry have a pair of transmembrane helices inserted into the P-loop NTPase domain [[cite:PUB00015187]].

The YodL-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YodL protein [swissprot:O30472], which is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, and is approximately 100 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (Y and D) that may be functionally important.

Pfam_Description: YoeB-like toxin of bacterial type II toxin-antitoxin system
Pfam_name: YoeB-like toxin of bacterial type II toxin-antitoxin system
Pfam_description: YoeB_toxin is a family of bacterial toxins that forms one component of the type II toxin-antitoxin system in E. coli whose antitoxin is represented by YefM, found in [pfam:PF02604]. The plasmid encoded Axe-Txe proteins in Enterococcus faecium act as an antitoxin-toxin pair. When the plasmid is lost, the antitoxin is degraded relatively quickly by host enzymes. This allows the toxin to interact with its intracellular target, thus killing the cell or impeding cell growth [[cite:PUB00015566]]. These toxins are highly potent protein synthesis inhibitors, specifically blocking the initiation of translation. In the case of YoeB, it binds to the 50 S ribosomal subunit in 70 S ribosomes and interacts with the A site leading to mRNA cleavage at this site. As a result, the 3'-end portion of the mRNA is released from ribosomes, and translation initiation is effectively inhibited [[cite:PUB00075545],[cite:PUB00075546]].

The YokU-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YokU protein [swissprot:C0H434] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 90 amino acids in length. There are two conserved CXXC sequence motifs. This is likely to be a family of bacterial antitoxins, as the sequence bears remote homology to the RelE fold family.

Members of this family are functionally uncharacterised. However it has been predicted that these proteins are functionally equivalent to the UmuD subunit of polymerase V from gram-negative bacteria [[cite:PUB00035492]]. This family has been shown to belong to the WYL-like superfamily [[cite:PUB00085051]].

YonK protein is expressed by the bacterial prophage SPbetaC [[cite:PUB00044553]]. It is a 63 residue protein that associates into a homo-octamer in the form of a beta-stranded barrel with four outer helical features at points of the compass. Its function is unknown.

Pfam_Description: Inner membrane component of T3SS, cytoplasmic domain
Pfam_name: Inner membrane component of T3SS, cytoplasmic domain
Pfam_description: Yop-YscD-cpl is the cytoplasmic domain of Yop proteins like YscD from Proteobacteria. YscD forms part of the inner membrane component of the bacterial type III secretion injectosome apparatus [[cite:PUB00020581],[cite:PUB00076171]].

Yop-YscD-ppl is the periplasmic domain of Yop proteins like YscD from Proteobacteria. YscD forms part of the inner membrane component of the bacterial type III secretion injectosome apparatus [[cite:PUB00020581],[cite:PUB00076172]]. This entry represents the first of three periplasmic BON domains [[cite:PUB00153859]].

Yop-YscD-ppl is the periplasmic domain of Yop proteins like YscD from Proteobacteria. YscD forms part of the inner membrane component of the bacterial type III secretion injectosome apparatus [[cite:PUB00020581],[cite:PUB00076172]]. This entry represents the second of three periplasmic BON domains.

Yop-YscD-ppl is the periplasmic domain of Yop proteins like YscD from Proteobacteria. YscD forms part of the inner membrane component of the bacterial type III secretion injectosome apparatus [[cite:PUB00020581],[cite:PUB00076172]]. This entry represents the third of three periplasmic BON domains.

This family consists of several bacterial YopD like proteins. Virulent Yersinia species harbour a common plasmid that encodes essential virulence determinants (Yersinia outer proteins [Yops]), which are regulated by the extracellular stimuli Ca2+ and temperature. YopD is thought to be a possible transmembrane protein and contains an amphipathic alpha-helix in its carboxy terminus [[cite:PUB00011518]].
The N terminal YopE domain targets YopE for secretion from the bacterium and translocation into eukaryotic cells [[cite:PUB00026901]].

The N-terminal domain of YopH is a compact structure composed of four alpha-helices and two beta-hairpins. Helices alpha-1 and alpha-3 are parallel to each other and antiparallel to helices alpha-2 and alpha-4. This domain targets YopH for secretion from the bacterium and translocation into eukaryotic cells, and has phosphotyrosyl peptide-binding activity, allowing for recognition of p130Cas and paxillin [[cite:PUB00028634]].
This hypothetical protein is expressed in bacteria, particularly Bacillus subtilis. It forms homo-dimers, with each monomer consisting of one alpha helix and three beta strands.
YopX is a protein that is largely helical, with three identical chains probably complexing into a twelve-chain structure.

The YoqO-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YoqO protein [swissprot:O31923], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria and viruses. Proteins in this family are approximately 120 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (I and Y) that may be functionally important.

YorP is a 71 residue protein found in bacteria. As it is also found in a bacteriophage it might be of viral origin. The structure is of an alpha helix between two of five beta strands. The function is unknown.

In yeast, Yos1 is a subunit of the Yip1p-Yif1p complex and is required for transport between the endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi complex. Yos1 appears to be conserved in eukaryotes[[cite:PUB00033378]].

This is the dimerization domain (DD) found in Yos9 proteins in yeast. Structural analysis revealed that this domain contributes to self association of Yos9. The overall fold of the domain can be classified as an alpha-beta-roll architecture, comprising two alpha-helices and seven beta-strands [[cite:PUB00059853]].

The YozD-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YozD protein [swissprot:O31863], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length.

This entry represents a domain found in the YozE-like family. YozE-like is a family of Firmicute proteins that carries a four-helix motif similar to sterile alpha motif (SAM) domains. The family is suggested to fall into two subfamilies, possibly with differing functions based on the different surface charges on the three structural representatives, YozE MW0776 and MW1311. What this function is is not yet known although it is likely to involve binding to DNA [[cite:PUB00075372]].

This is the N-terminal region of YpeB, a protein restricted to endospore-forming species in the Firmicutes lineage of bacteria, that have been found in all such species to date except Clostridium perfringens. YpeB and the spore-cortex-lytic enzyme SleB are required for normal germination [[cite:PUB00100161]]. This protein is essential in stabilising SleB enzyme in Bacillus spores, and may regulate its activity during germination [[cite:PUB00100161]].

Pfam_Description: YpeB sporulation, PepSY1 and PepSY2 domains
Pfam_name: YpeB sporulation, PepSY1 and PepSY2 domains
Pfam_description: YpeB is a sporulation protein that, together with the spore-cortex-lytic enzyme SleB, is required for normal germination. YpeB stabilises SleB enzyme and may regulate its activity during spore germination [[cite:PUB00014275],[cite:PUB00152410],[cite:PUB00151941],[cite:PUB00151942],[cite:PUB00151943],[cite:PUB00100161]]. It consists of three tandemly repeated PepSY domains at the C-terminal, being the first two (PepSY1 and PepSY2) represented in this entry and the last one in [pfam:PF03413].

This entry represents a family of proteins (previously known as FAM72) that is distantly related to and named after the drosophila Yippee, a zinc-binding protein [[cite:PUB00020578]]. In contrast to the other Yippee-like proteins [[cite:PUB00078711]], this family of proteins possesses some distinct features such as the presence of a second putative zinc binding site that is unique to them. The constituent zinc coordinating residues of this second site are invariant within the family suggesting that this is likely a genuine zinc binding site. This family of proteins is found in eukaryotes.

The YpjP-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YpjP protein [swissprot:P54172] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 200 amino acids in length.

Members of this family of Yersinia pseudo-tuberculosis mitogens adopt a sandwich structure consisting of nine strands in two beta sheets, in a jelly-roll topology. As with other super-antigens, they are able to excessively activate T cells by binding to the T cell receptor [[cite:PUB00029905]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.
This family of proteins contains the B. subtilis YpoC protein [swissprot:P39789]. It is largely confined to bacilli bacteria.

The YppF-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YppF protein [swissprot:P50834], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length. There is a conserved LLDF sequence motif.

The YppG-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YppG protein [swissprot:P50835], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 115 and 181 amino acids in length. There are two completely conserved residues (F and G) that may be functionally important.

Family in the SLOG superfamily showing fusions to NAD utilization and ADP-ribosylation domains including NUDIX, NADAR and MACRO. Members of this family are predicted to function as sensors of nucleotide, nucleotide-derived ligands, or nucleic acids, which are potentially processed/modified by the associating enzymes [[cite:PUB00091021]].

The YpzG-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YpzG protein [swissprot:C0H444] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 50 amino acids in length. There is a conserved QVNG sequence motif.

The YpzI-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YpzI protein [swissprot:C0H446] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 40 amino acids in length.
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.
This hypothetical protein is expressed in bacteria, particularly Bacillus subtilis. It forms a homo-dimer, with each monomer containing an alpha helix and four beta strands.

This protein family is found in many different bacterial species but is of viral origin. The protein forms an oligomer and functions as a processive alkaline exonuclease that digests linear double-stranded DNA in a Mg(2+)-dependent reaction, It has a preference for 5'-phosphorylated DNA ends. It thus forms part of the two-component SynExo viral recombinase functional unit [[cite:PUB00044555]].
This N-terminal domain is found in Bacillus and related spp. The function is not known.
This entry represents the HeH domain of the uncharacterised protein YqbF from Bacillus subtilis.

This entry represents a domain found standalone in the Uncharacterized protein YqbQ, Phage-like element PBSX protein XkdQ and other related proteins. This domain is also found N-terminal in Clostridioides difficile endolysin (Ecd09610). It is predicted to adopt a globular structure comprised mainly of two beta-barrels arranged in a head-to-tail manner. The function of this domain is unknown.
This family of proteins are functionally uncharacterised. The family include YqcI and YcgG from B. subtilis. The alignment contains a conserved FPC motif at the N-terminus and CPF at the C-terminus.
This entry includes the E. coli YqeC protein. This protein belongs to the P-loop superfamily.

This entry is found at the C-terminal of Nitric oxide-associated protein 1 (NOA1) from animals and rice, BPG2 from Arabidopsis and YqeH from B. subtilis. YqeH is an orthologue of NOA1. This domain has a beta-sandwich structure with homology to the RNA-binding regulator TRAP, and the hypoxia factor pVHL. The residues for RNA recognition in TRAP are conserved in members of this entry, suggesting that these are G-proteins that may regulate nucleic acid recognition [[cite:PUB00051653]].
The function of this domain found in the YqeY protein is uncertain.

Pfam_Description: Putative stage IV sporulation protein YqfD
Pfam_name: Putative stage IV sporulation protein YqfD
Pfam_description: This family consists of several putative bacterial stage IV sporulation (SpoIV) proteins. YqfD of Bacillus subtilis ([swissprot:P54469]) is known to be essential for efficient sporulation although its exact function is unknown [[cite:PUB00012907]].

The YqfQ-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YqfQ protein [swissprot:P54474], also known as VrrA, which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 146 and 237 amino acids in length. There are two conserved sequence motifs: QYGP and PKLY.
YqgB encodes adaptive factors that acts in synergy with vqfZ , enabling the bacteria to cope with the physical environment in vivo, facilitating colonisation of the host [[cite:PUB00046099]].
This is a family of unknown function found in Enterobacteriaceae such as E.coli and Shigella.

The YqgF domain of SPT6 proteins is homologous to the E.coli RuvC [[cite:PUB00065451]] but its putative catalytic site lacks the carboxylate side chains critical for coordinating magnesium ions that mediate phosphodiester bond-cleavage [[cite:PUB00067478]]

This family consists of several short bacterial proteins, including Uncharacterized protein YqgQ from Bacillus subtilis. YqgQ folds into a three-helical bundle, with the helix order being left-handed and with the third helix flanked by a loop. Based on sequence and structural homology, this protein is thought to be involved in single-stranded nucleic acid binding [[cite:PUB00101010]].
This entry represents a beta propeller domain found in the B. subtilis YqgU protein. The proteins in this family contain an N-terminal lipid attachment motif suggesting they are lipoproteins.

Pfam_Description: Bacterial protein YqhG of unknown function
Pfam_name: Bacterial protein YqhG of unknown function
Pfam_description: This family of putative proteins is conserved in the Bacillaceae family of the Firmicutes. The function is not known.
This family is conserved in the Bacillaceae family of the Firmicutes. The function is not known.
This entry represents a presumed helical domain found at the N-terminal of several bacterial proteins, including the inner membrane protein YqiJ from E. coli, whose function is not clear.
This entry represents the OB-fold domain found in several bacterial proteins, including the inner membrane protein YqiJ from E. coli, whose function is not clear.

The YqjK-like protein family includes the E. coli YqjK protein [swissprot:Q47710] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length. There is a single completely conserved residue R that may be functionally important.

The YqzE-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YqzE protein [swissprot:O32020], which is functionally uncharacterised. It is a part of the ComG operon, which is regulated by the competence transcription factor ComK [[cite:PUB00057382]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 49 and 66 amino acids in length.

The YqzH-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YqzH protein [swissprot:O32014], which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 60 amino acids in length.

The YqzL-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YqzL protein [swissprot:C0H452] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 50 amino acids in length.

The YqzM-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YqzM protein [swissprot:C0H453] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 40 amino acids in length.

This is a family of proteins that are activated by PhoP. PhoP protein controls the expression of a large number of genes that mediate adaptation to low Mg2+ environments and/or virulence in several bacterial species. YbrL is proposed to be acting in a loop activity with PhoP and PrmA analogous to the multicomponent loop in Salmonella where the PhoP-dependent PmrD protein activates the regulatory protein PmrA, and the activated PmrA then represses transcription from the PmrD promoter which harbours binding sites for both the PhoP and PmrA proteins. Expression of YrbL is induced in low Mg2+ in a PhoP-dependent fashion and repressed by Fe3+ in a PmrA-dependent manner [[cite:PUB00044556]].

The YrhC-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YrhC protein [swissprot:O05395] which is functionally uncharacterised. YrhC is on the same operon as the MccA and MccB genes, which are involved in the conversion of methionine to cysteine. Expression of this operon is repressed in the presence of sulphate or cysteine [[cite:PUB00057337]]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 80 amino acids in length.

The YrhK-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YrhK protein [swissprot:O05401] which is functionally uncharacterised. Its expression is under the control of the motility sigma factor sigma-D [[cite:PUB00057339]]. This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, and is approximately 60 amino acids in length.
This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 236 and 351 amino acids in length. The member from Bacillus subtilis, UniProtKB:O05411, is named YrpD.
YrvL prevents expression and activity of the YrvI sigma factor. It may function as an anti-sigma factor [[cite:PUB00056157],[cite:PUB00058233]]
This is a family of unknown function found in Bacillus.

The YrzO-like protein family includes the B. subtilis YrzO protein [swissprot:C0H458] which is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 50 amino acids in length.

This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. These proteins are related to E.coli YsaB [swissprot:Q0TBP2]. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are approximately 100 amino acids in length. These proteins are lipoproteins.

Ysc84 is a family of Las17-binding proteins found in metazoa.
